name: Mood Boards
description:
A mood board is a curated collection of images, colours, materials, typography, textures and other references assembled to explore the intended experiential or aesthetic direction of a design.

Mood boards can help teams discuss qualities that are difficult to communicate verbally and compare different interpretations before committing to a detailed visual language.
whenToUse: Use mood boards when exploring visual, material or experiential direction and when collaborators need a shared vocabulary for qualities such as atmosphere, character or tone.
steps: Define the experience or qualities being explored.
Gather a broad range of visual and material references.
Avoid limiting references to products identical to the one being designed.
Group references that express related qualities.
Curate the collection to create a coherent direction.
Translate selected qualities into design decisions rather than copying individual references.
lookOutFor: A mood board should communicate more than a fashionable aesthetic.
Avoid uncritical use of copyrighted imagery in published work.
Ensure that visual references do not introduce cultural stereotypes or associations that have not been considered.

resources.citation: Lucero, A. (2012). “Framing, Aligning, Paradoxing, Abstracting, and Directing: How Design Mood Boards Work.” *Proceedings of DIS 2012*.
